newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks drift lower in morning after strong open.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks drift lower in morning after strong open.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks retreated from initial gains to trade slightly lower on Wednesday morning due to profit-taking in property stocks following the recent sharp gains in that sector, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index eased 35 points, or 0.26 percent, to 13,543 after touching a high of 13,627.49 just after the open.
Turnover was heavy at HK$3.41 billion.
"There is a little bit of profit-taking going on in property stocks," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston. "We are still following Wall Street, which had a flat day."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average inched ahead 10.83 points to a new record close of 7.225.32 overnight.
In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.25 to HK$90.50 while Cheung Kong was unchanged at HK$73.00 and Henderson gained HK$0.25 to HK$70.25.
Hong Kong Telecom added HK$0.25 to HK$14.35.
"There is still strong buying of Telecom carried over from yesterday," Verin said.
Brokers said there was big buying in Telecom shares from brokerages such as Peregrine and CEF GC on Tuesday.
G.K. Goh Securities expects Hongkong Telecom to announce an 8.7 percent rise in net profit to HK$10.8 billion for the year ended March 31 when the company reports its final results on Thursday.
Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities, said a consolidation was healthy following the recent sharp gains on the Hang Seng.
"The market has discounted the interest rate rise factor, the property market has been bottomed out and there are funds continuing to move in from Southeast Asia," he said.
Brokers noted active buying in H shares, which pushed up the Hang Seng Chinese Enterprise Index of 26-listed mainland companies by 11 points, or 1.07 percent, to 1,122.
H share Jilin Chemical added HK$0.20 to HK$1.62 on heavy turnover of HK$252 million.
Among the red chips, CITIC Pacific added HK$0.20 to HK$43.00 and China Overseas rose HK$0.125 to HK$4.375.
